method: Extracted full paragraph text from ten live repository article files. Source evidence is not sufficient to certify every assertion; all extracted paragraphs remain pending primary-source checks.

paragraphs.text: The anime adaptation of Keigo Shinzo's manga will air on NHK General in January 2027.
Hirayasumi is confirmed for January 2027 on NHK General in Japan. The exact day and international streaming platform remain unannounced.

Yuma Uchida voices Hiroto Ikuta, Mayu Takahashi voices Natsumi Kobayashi and Rikako Aikawa voices Hanae Wada. Production +h. animates the series. Kei Suezawa directs and writes the scripts, Naoyuki Asano designs characters, Mika Nishimura is art director and Kaori Sawada composes music.

VIZ Media's new teaser and cast reveal provide the first character performances. An early episode screening was scheduled for October 7, 2026 in New York, ahead of the Japanese TV broadcast. The preview is not an international streaming release.
The story follows carefree Hiroto and his cousin Natsumi as they navigate ordinary life, friendships and family around the house Hiroto inherited from a neighbor.
NHK General is confirmed in Japan. Streaming platforms and territories outside Japan are not confirmed.
Is the exact January date known? No, only the month is confirmed.Is the trailer official? Yes, the VIZ teaser above is for this adaptation.Is international streaming confirmed? Not yet.
Walking Home with You (Houkago Kitaku Biyori) premieres in April 2027 on Nippon TV. The newly confirmed TV window arrives with the anime's first teaser visual.
The anime is officially scheduled to begin airing on Nippon TV in April 2027. An exact premiere day has not yet been announced.

The adaptation now has both a confirmed television format and release month. The announcement also introduced the first anime teaser visual, turning the earlier adaptation announcement into a concrete Spring 2027 release target.

Mai Matsuda's school romantic comedy follows Shun Sato, a new high-school student who gave up his soccer dream after an injury, and his unusual upperclassman Naoki Sato. Their relationship develops through the so-called Hyper Going-Home Club and the everyday detours they share after school.
Those details remain unconfirmed as of the April 2027 announcement. AniNextUp will update this guide when the production committee announces the Japanese cast, principal staff or animation studio.
Nippon TV is confirmed for the Japanese broadcast. No international streaming service has been officially announced yet, so any global platform listing remains pending.

No anime PV or trailer specific to the TV series was announced with this update. The official material currently centers on the teaser visual; this page will be updated when an official promotional video becomes available.
The next useful announcements are an exact April premiere date, cast and production staff, animation studio, an official PV and international streaming availability.

Pokémon Horizons: Season 4—Wonders Ahead now has a firm U.S. streaming date. Part 1 premieres on Netflix on February 27, 2027, with Liko and Roy returning for the next chapter of the current Pokémon anime.

Part 1 of Pokémon Horizons: Season 4—Wonders Ahead premieres February 27, 2027 in the United States. The Pokémon Company International announced the date on October 6 alongside the season's official trailer.

In the United States, Netflix is the confirmed exclusive streaming home for Part 1. The announcement specifically confirms the U.S. release, so viewers elsewhere should wait for territory-specific availability rather than assume the same date applies everywhere.

The update gave the English-language season its official Wonders Ahead subtitle, locked in the February 27 Netflix date for the U.S. and released a new official trailer. The Pokémon Company also confirmed that additional Season 4 episodes will arrive later, although dates for later parts have not been announced.

Season 4 continues with Liko and Roy after the Laquium threat. Their travels open into a new stretch of exploration and battles as they meet more Trainers and Pokémon. The new material also highlights Navie and Ditto among the encounters ahead.

Wonders Ahead continues the existing Pokémon Horizons story rather than rebooting it. Netflix already carries the first three seasons in the U.S., making them the clearest catch-up path before Part 1 arrives.
An episode count for the February batch has not been officially announced. The confirmed information is the Part 1 date and that more Season 4 episodes will follow in the future.
The fantasy romance begins today on Crunchyroll, following Rose, a solitary witch whose longtime crush asks her to brew a love potion for someone else.
Episode 1 premiered October 5, 2026. Crunchyroll's current simulcast calendar lists the premiere at 8:30 a.m. PT. Release displays can vary by territory and local time zone.

Rose lives quietly as the Good Witch of the Lake. Her four-year crush on Royal Knight Harij seems doomed when he asks her to make a love potion. Rose agrees, stretching out the ingredient-gathering process so she can spend more time with him, only for their relationship to begin changing in unexpected ways.

This is a new TV anime adaptation of Eiko Mutsuhana's light novels, so viewers do not need to watch an earlier anime first. The story mixes fantasy and romance and starts from Rose and Harij's unusual love-potion request.

Mikako Komatsu voices Rose and Yohei Azakami voices Harij. Keizo Kusakawa directs at Diomedéa, Wataru Watari handles series composition, Masakazu Ishikawa handles character design, and Satoshi Matsumura composes the music.
Crunchyroll lists the series in its Fall 2026 simulcast catalog. Availability can vary by country, so viewers should check the service in their territory.
Latest update: October 5, 2026. AniNextUp uses confirmed release information and leaves unannounced details pending.
Maomao and Jinshi return in a completely original theatrical mystery on December 11, 2026.

The Apothecary Diaries: Treasure of the Late Empress opens in Japanese theaters on December 11, 2026. The movie is a theatrical project with a completely original mystery rather than a simple compilation of television episodes.

Yes. Original author Natsu Hyuuga provides the story concept. Maomao and Jinshi become involved in a mystery connected to a deceased consort, a southern water city, pirates and a hidden treasure, giving the film its own storyline within the series' world.
Norio Naganuma directs, Yuko Kakihara handles the screenplay and TOHO animation STUDIO produces the animation. Aoi Yuki returns as Maomao and Takeo Otsuka as Jinshi.

The December 11 date currently refers to the Japanese theatrical release. No international streaming date has been announced, so AniNextUp will keep cinema and streaming availability separate until an official release plan is confirmed.
TOHO theatrical release lineup · TOHO official film and Season 3 production announcement · Crunchyroll international theatrical distribution announcement

Takopi's Original Sin: Thank You, See You Tomorrow opens in Japanese theaters on November 27, 2026. The theatrical version revisits the complete television anime while adding material created specifically for the movie presentation.

The film is a theatrical re-edit of all six episodes of the Takopi's Original Sin anime and includes newly added scenes. It therefore is not a separate sequel, but it offers additional material beyond simply screening the original episodes unchanged.

Takopi is an alien who arrives on Earth hoping to spread happiness. After meeting Shizuka, he uses mysterious Happy Gadgets in an attempt to restore her smile, only to discover that the problems surrounding her family and school life cannot be solved with simple magical tools.
The November 27 release is currently confirmed for Japanese cinemas. An international theatrical or streaming release has not been announced.
Armored Trooper VOTOMS: The Gray Witch Part 1 opens November 20, 2026 in Japan. Mamoru Oshii directs the new Sunrise theatrical anime.

Armored Trooper VOTOMS: The Gray Witch Part 1 opens in Japanese theaters on November 20, 2026. It is the first half of a new two-part theatrical project; a release date for Part 2 has not yet been announced.

The story is set near the end of the Hundred Year War and follows an investigation into Ash Vamps, a soldier nicknamed the Witch because she repeatedly returns alive from missions that kill the rest of her unit. The premise returns VOTOMS to its military science-fiction roots while introducing a new central mystery.
Mamoru Oshii directs the project. Sunrise produces the animation with production cooperation from Production I.G, while Bandai Namco Filmworks handles distribution.
The November 20 date is for the Japanese theatrical release. No international streaming platform has been confirmed, so AniNextUp will not list one until an official announcement is made.
Witch on the Holy Night opens in Japanese theaters November 20, 2026. The ufotable film receives an international theatrical release beginning January 2027.
Witch on the Holy Night opens in Japanese theaters on November 20, 2026. The film adapts TYPE-MOON's visual novel and brings another major TYPE-MOON project to animation studio ufotable.

Aoko Aozaki appears to be an ordinary high school student, but she is actually an apprentice Magician. She lives with Alice Kuonji while training to become a full-fledged Magician, and the arrival of Soujuurou Shizuki changes the balance of their lives. The official introduction frames the movie as the beginning of Aoko's story.

The original work is credited to Kinoko Nasu and TYPE-MOON, with ufotable handling animation production and screenplay production. Masaru Takeuchi directs, Moe Tsuzuki serves as character designer, and Hikaru Kondo is chief director. Hideyuki Fukasawa composes the music.
The final trailer confirmed supercell for the theme song “Yoru to Ao.” The main cast includes Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki, Kana Hanazawa as Alice Kuonji and Yusuke Kobayashi as Soujuurou Shizuki.

The November 20 date is the Japanese theatrical release. The international theatrical rollout follows in January 2027, including January 28 in confirmed Latin American markets and January 29 in the United States and Canada, while a streaming date has not been confirmed. AniNextUp will keep theatrical and streaming availability separate so an international cinema announcement is not mistaken for an online release.
The sequel to Expelled from Paradise opens in Japanese theaters on November 13, 2026.
Rakuen Tsuihou: Kokoro no Resonance opens in Japanese theaters on November 13, 2026. It is the long-awaited sequel to the 2014 science-fiction anime film Expelled from Paradise.

The sequel returns to the conflict between the virtual society of DEVA and life on Earth. Gabriel and other agents pursue the mysterious Fallen—former security personnel who escaped to the surface after the events involving Angela Balzac—expanding the world established by the first movie.

Seiji Mizushima returns as director and Gen Urobuchi writes the screenplay. Masatsugu Saito handles character design, NARASAKI composes the music and Toei Animation produces the film, reuniting core creative staff from the original project.

The November 13 date currently refers specifically to the Japanese theatrical release. An international streaming date has not been announced, so AniNextUp is keeping theatrical and streaming availability separate until an official platform announcement is made.
Demon's Crest premieres worldwide November 6, 2026, exclusively on Prime Video.

Demon's Crest premieres worldwide on November 6, 2026. Unlike many seasonal anime with separate Japanese and international schedules, the official site explicitly describes the release as a worldwide Prime Video exclusive.

Prime Video has worldwide exclusive streaming rights beginning November 6. That makes the platform the confirmed destination for the anime rather than a Japan-only broadcaster followed by an unconfirmed international simulcast.

Sixth-grader Yuuma Ashihara takes part in a test of Actual Magic, a full-sensory full-dive VRMMO. After Yuuma and his classmates defeat a boss and try to log out, the boundary between the game's world and reality begins to collapse.

Production I.G is producing the adaptation of Reki Kawahara's light novel series. Kawahara is also known for Sword Art Online and Accel World. The official promotional campaign pairs the virtual-world imagery of Actual Magic with an increasingly unsettling real-world setting.
Ado performs the opening theme “Shinka.” The production later confirmed Soala's “ReaL” as the ending theme alongside its second promotional video.
